title.narrative: Saint Lucia Health System Strengthening Project

description.narrative: The development objective is to improve the accessibility, efficiency, and responsiveness of key health services, and provide a response in the event of eligible crises or emergencies.

The development objective of the Health System Strengthening Project for Saint Lucia is to improve the accessibility, efficiency, and responsiveness of key health services. The project comprises of four components. The first component, design and implementation of an essential benefits package focuses on the demand side and includes the review of the design and implementation of the benefits package, including administration, purchasing and contracting arrangements, regulations surrounding the scheme, and potential sources of additional revenue for expanding health service coverage. It consists of following sub-components: (i) review of the essential benefits package; and (ii) implementation of the essential benefits package. The second component, strengthening service delivery in support of the essential benefits package consists of following sub-components: (i) improving service delivery through performance-based financing (PBF); (ii) strengthening the supply of health care services; and (iii) public health emergency preparedness and response. The third component, institutional capacity building, project management, and coordination will cover project implementation efforts, including project management, fiduciary tasks, and monitoring and evaluation (M and E) associated with supervision of the project. The fourth component, contingent emergency response component (CERC) will provide funding following an eligible emergency. It will include conditions for the use of funds, and will only be triggered when certain actions, as agreed by the government and the Bank are met.

condition.narrative: Section I. Implementation Arrangements. A. 2. (a). MOHW Project Implementation Unit ("MOHW-PIU"). The Recipient shall maintain atall times until the completion of the Project the MOHW-PIU within MOHW, with staff, terms of reference, mandate and resourcessatisfactory to the Association; including a Project Manager, a PBF Coordinator, a financial management specialist, a procurementspecialist, and a monitoring and evaluation specialist, all with experience, qualifications, expertise and terms of referenceacceptable to the Association.

Section III.B of Schedule 2:Original Financing Agreement is amended: under Category (2) until and unless the Association hasreceived adequate evidence that: (a) the four Management Agreements have been signed and are in effect; (b) the PBF CounterVerification Agreement has been signed and is in effect (c) the PBF OM has been adopted; all in form and substance satisfactory tothe Association

Section III.B.1(c) of Schedule 2: Notwithstanding the provisions of Part A above, no withdrawal shall be made for EmergencyExpenditures under Category (3), unless and until the Association is satisfied, and has notified the Recipient of its satisfaction,that all of the following conditions have been met in respect of said expenditures: (i) the Recipient has determined that anEligible Emergency has occurred, has furnished to the Association a request to include the proposed activities in the EmergencyResponse Part in order to respond to said emergency, and the Association has agreed with such determination, accepted said requestand notified the Recipient thereof; (ii) the Recipient has ensured that all safeguard instruments required for said activitieshave been prepared and disclosed, and the Recipient has ensured that any actions which are required to be taken under saidinstruments have been implemented, all in accordance with the provisions of Section I.F of this Schedule; (iii) the entities incharge of coordinating and implementing the Emergency Response Part have adequate staff and resources, in accordance with theprovisions of Section I.F of this Schedule, for the purposes of said activities; and (iv) the Recipient has adopted the CERCManual, in form and substance acceptable to the Association, and the provisions of the CERC Manual remain - or have been updated inaccordance with the provisions of Section I.F of this Schedule so as to be - appropriate for the inclusion and implementation ofthe Emergency Response Part.

title.narrative: Percentage of persons in the ATP living with Diabetes who are managed by the PBF facilities, according to OM protocols

comment.narrative: MET. Values of blood pressure, weight, height, BMI and prescriptions (attributes) were not consistently recorded. The following steps were taken: •Short-term consultancy to complete data entry in SLUHIS. 4 Data Entry Clerks were hired and trained in July 2025. Significant improvement seen due to the updating of outstanding information in SLUHIS resulting in over 50% of the target being reached as of Sept 2025. •Scale-up of Behavioural Change Communication programmes, education and sensitization among men is necessary at the community (townhall meetings) level to increase access to care. •Heighten tracking of follow-up appointments to enable a proactive approach to delinquency among patients.

title.narrative: Percentage of Primary Health Care facilities participating in the Performance Based Financing (PBF) scheme that have developed Work plans based on the results of the quarterly satisfaction surveys

comment.narrative: MET Sept 2025, indicator revised as part of the restructuring to give clear indication that both the client interview exit and client quarterly satisfaction surveys applies to the 8 Phase 1 PBF facilities and 9 Phase 2 PBF Facilities, as such the target was changed from 60 to 100%. The results based on findings from both the client interview exit survey (quarterly) and the client satisfaction survey (semi-annual) will inform progress and decision making. After an 8-month delay in implementation, renegotiations with the Consultant for the Client Satisfaction Survey was finalized in July 2025, and resulted with an amendment to Contract #128. The addendum was dated July 25th, 2025 and indicates that the Consultancy starts on August 1 and ended on September 30 2025. Phase1 facilities were covered under Contract #128 Consultancy. The sample size was 908 human subjects. The client interview exit surveys (Contract #114) were conducted for all 17 Facilities over the period Nov 2024-May 2025

title.narrative: Number of public sector providers registered under the PBF scheme

comment.narrative: MET June 2024. Eight (8) Participating Facilities in the PBF Pilot Phase 1 signed the Management Agreement on 29th June 2023, they are, Mon Repos Wellness Centre, La Croix Wellness Centre, Jacmel Wellness Centre, Richford Wellness Centre, Dennery Hospital, Soufriere Hospital, La Fargue Wellness Centre, Desruisseaux Wellness Centre. Nine (9) additional facilities were launched in June 2024 of which 2 (Delcer and Canaries Wellness Centers) will be SMARTed under the OECS Regional Health Project. Discussions with the MOHWEA on specific operative plans, and deadlines remain ongoing. The Signing of the Management Agreement by Regional Supervisors took place on June 5th 2024. The nine (9) Phase 2 Facilities are, Delcer, Canaries, Anse La Raye, Vanard, Ti Rocher, Mongouge, Etangs, Micoud and Fond St Jacque Wellness Centers.

title.narrative: Compliance with 2005 International Health Regulations (IHR) by maintaining a trained Rapid Response Team (RRT) to respond to events that may constitute a public health emergency

comment.narrative: MET. This is one of the key actions which the Government is asked to comply with on a yearly basis by the World Health Organization (WHO) as a critical activity under the 13 core capacity areas of the 2005 International Health Regulations (IHR). The desired results for this PDO have been met by the efforts of the Implementation Agency. Due to the COVID-19 pandemic and the need for strengthening national response, regional health agencies such as CARPHA and PAHO held online virtual training for the Rapid Response Team (including Contact Tracing, Infection Prevention and Control and Field Epidemiology) to respond to the public health emergencies.

title.narrative: Number of persons in the ATP not diagnosed with Hypertension screened at the PBF participating facilities based on national protocols

comment.narrative: 88% achieved. The potential encounters in which screening occurs encompass both outpatient and emergency encounters. (For example, if a patient fails to receive screening for hypertension through their regular outpatient visits, but is screened during an emergency visit, that patient should count as having been screened for hypertension in the construction of this indicator). RMI data training and Goal setting training by the PBFU to the PBF Executive team and Supervisors took place in January 2025. As of September 30, 2025 this indicator has achieved 88% of its target.

title.narrative: People receiving quality health, nutrition, and population services

comment.narrative: SURPASSED. During this last ISR period the CRI reporting improved due to improved HIS data and a more precise definition of the services. This data is generated and extracted from SLUHIS Database. The results represent number of persons receiving Quality, Health, Nutrition and Populations Services at 34 Wellness Centers. Catchment area of 34 facilities (denominator) and ATP criteria (unique encounter) for numerator, to better reflect service coverage. On assumption that we would want persons to visit a facility at least twice a year. The population now stand at 171,840 yielding an expected 343,680 encounters.
